market_holds: Spot $0.80 (sealed baseline 2026-11-20), about $42m market cap on ~51.4m shares, against cash and deposits of $21.4m at end-June (Q2 release). No options market and no usable EDGAR reaction history in the baseline. Its own past print days, from Yahoo daily bars: Nov-2025 -13.9% close-to-close, Feb-2026 -30% (the founder also left that day), May-2026 opened -6.6% and closed +2.7%, Aug-2026 opened +12.6% and closed +23.7% on 7m shares. So the usual move is double digits. The stock bled from $1.67 after the Q2 print to $0.60 on 2026-11-05, then bounced 37% to $0.80-0.82 (20d +8%). It got a Nasdaq bid-price deficiency letter on 2026-11-10, with compliance due 2027-05-10. Q3 KPIs were pre-released 2026-10-15 well above the guide (GBV $437m against a $390-397m guide, transactions 494k against 481-490k), and the stock did not move that day. Q3 guide from 2026-08-17: revenue $7.7-7.8m, adj. EBITDA -$1.3m to -$1.2m. FY guide: revenue $30.4-31.0m, adj. EBITDA -$6.9m to -$6.4m, breakeven by Q4 2026. Aggregator consensus (undated): Q3 revenue $7.7m (Benzinga) or $7.90m (Chartmill), EPS -$0.05. Turnover is about $65k a day.
view: This is a $42m freight-software company with roughly half its market cap in cash. The platform KPIs are pre-released, so the print turns on three things the KPIs do not show: Solutions/SaaS revenue (about 62% of revenue, down 4% YoY in Q2 on SaaS weakness), the EBITDA path to the promised Q4 breakeven, and cash. The Q2 setup is the closest analogue. Then a GBV beat of about 8% over the guide became revenue of $7.7m against a $7.2-7.4m guide, and the stock rose 24%. In Q3 the GBV beat is larger, about 10-12% over the guide, but the guide itself already assumed +16-18% GBV. My own arithmetic: platform revenue at Q2's ~0.69% of GBV gives about $3.0m, against $2.6m a year ago. That makes total revenue about $7.8m with flat Solutions ($4.8m) and $7.6-7.7m if Solutions slips further against a strong $5.1m comparison from Q3 2025. So the likely revenue outcome is at to slightly above the guide and the higher consensus, not a Q2-sized beat. The Q3 KPI release added a line that Solutions are 'less directly reflected' in the KPIs and would be updated with the results. That reads as a hedge, and the founder's proxy campaign cites pricing pressure on SaaS renewals. Against that, EBITDA is guided to a steep improvement from cost cuts and should land near the guide, and a reaffirmed Q4 breakeven at an EV of about $20m could pull in bottom-fishers on a thin float, as in August. Other cross-currents inside the window: a founder proxy fight at the 2026-12-16 AGM, a possible reverse-split announcement, and a 37% two-week rebound that has already taken some of the setup. I lean slightly up because the cost path and the GBV beat favour at-or-above-guide numbers and the stock trades near cash. But I cannot show a gap the price does not hold, and the Solutions line, which decides the print, is the one I cannot see.

recommendation.reason: The pre-released GBV and transaction beat is public, and my rebuild of revenue from those KPIs lands only at to slightly above the guide, because Solutions, the majority line, is not in the KPIs and has been the weak spot. There is no dated, independent evidence on Solutions or SaaS for Q3, so I cannot say the price is behind on the deciding line. The probability stays well below the 65 threshold.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Solutions revenue flat or up YoY with a reaffirmed or raised Q4 breakeven and FY revenue guide (long case), or Solutions down high single digits with a softened breakeven or a financing or reverse-split announcement (short case).

self_critique: The Q2 analogue was a large KPI beat that became a revenue and EBITDA beat and a +24% day, with the stock similarly depressed going in. Q3's GBV beat is even larger, the market ignored it on 10-15, and the stock is near cash, so a clean beat plus a reaffirmed breakeven could again produce +15-25%. Leaning only 55 may be too timid. On the other side, the 37% two-week rebound and the Solutions hedge in the KPI release could mean the downside is the one less priced.
approach_notes: The P4 'priced is a claim to prove' framing and rebuilding the line from KPIs (P3 own arithmetic) were the most useful steps; they showed that the GBV beat does not reach Solutions. On a thin-coverage FPI there were no fresh stakeholder traces for the deciding line, so P8's early stop applied.
